title: per-route latency heatmap + adaptive alerting and streaming partial-response traces
author: Marisol Rivera
description: Motivation: customers have asked for better per-route visibility into where compute/time is spent (batching vs decoding vs KV cache lookups) and too many noisy latency alerts for ephemeral traffic patterns. This PR: 1) adds a low-cardinality per-route latency heatmap metric that buckets p50/p90/p99 across request path + sequence-length bands, 2) instruments streaming partial-response traces so long-running streaming requests emit incremental spans (start/segment/end) and include batch_key, shard, and kv_cache_hit boolean as span attributes, 3) introduces an adaptive alerting baseline for token-level latency SLOs using a 28-day sliding median + MAD based threshold to suppress transient spikes, 4) exposes a derived metric "route_token_cost_estimate" (tokens * per-token-cost-gauge) for dashboarding and chargeback, and 5) ships a Grafana dashboard (request-path-latency-heatmap) and alert rule updates tuned for reduced noise. Important design notes: - The heatmap is implemented as Prometheus histogram vectors with controlled label cardinality: route_id, seq_band (0-128,129-512,513+), model_family. We intentionally avoid per-customer labels here to prevent unbounded series. - Streaming traces use the OTLP span exporter through the collector; spans are emitted at segment boundaries with a small metadata envelope to avoid amplifying trace volume. Sampling policy: by default 1% of requests are fully sampled; requests that hit p95+p99 latency are sampled at higher rate for root-cause analysis. - Adaptive alerts run in the alertmanager as a recording rule that computes baseline = median(last_28d) and threshold = baseline + max(2 * MAD, 50ms). This reduces pager noise during controlled rollout windows. Checklist: - [x] Add Prometheus histograms and labels - [x] Add OTLP trace segment emission - [x] Add route_token_cost_estimate derived metric - [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON and panels - [x] Add recording rules for adaptive baseline - [x] Update docs/observability with config knobs - [x] Unit + integration tests for histogram bucket correctness Backwards compatibility: Metric names are additive; existing dashboards continue to work. Alert semantics changed (re-tuning) — ops were notified on ENG-ops prior to merge. Related: ENG-2197 (token SLO refactor), SUP-9421 (customer incident that motivated heatmap). Deployment notes: - Requires collector config change (new receiver route for streaming spans) and Grafana provisioning. - Rolling deploy of the serving runtime is safe; histograms are additive and missing labels are handled. - After deployment, monitor prometheus series cardinality in the first 48h (we've added an internal debug counter to emit series estimates).

review_comments: Ethan Li (2026-02-13): Nice work on the sampling policy. A couple of asks: can we document how to increase sampling for a specific customer during incident triage? Also, please add a comment explaining the choice of MAD vs stddev.

Marisol Rivera (2026-02-13): Reply: Added a short runbook section in docs/observability/per-route-heatmaps.md describing how to bump sampling for an organization_id via the debug endpoint. Also added comment about MAD's robustness to non-Gaussian latency distributions.
Priya Suresh (2026-02-14): Small nit: seq_band '513+' label might be better named '513-2048' if we plan to split further. Is it expensive to add another band?

Marisol Rivera (2026-02-14): Reply: We kept coarse bands to limit series growth; if customers request finer granularity we'll add a config knob in charts/observability/values.yaml to enable an extra band behind a flag.
Dmitri Volkov (2026-02-16): CI flaky test 'TestOTLPBatching' failed once; I reran the job and it passed. Approving on green.
Ops (ENG-ops) (2026-02-17): Confirmed alert noise reduction on staging. Please ensure the prometheus retention is at least 30d in prod or adaptive baselines will be inaccurate.
release_notes: Added per-route latency heatmaps, streaming partial-response tracing, adaptive baseline alerting for token-level latency SLOs, and a new Grafana dashboard. Reduced alert noise and added a route-level token cost estimate metric for chargeback.
